fields.name: DIVLD
fields.text: Read-only; reset clears it and the first write to FCDIV sets it, whatever value is written.

values.text: FCDIV not written since reset; FLASH erase and program are blocked.
FCDIV written since reset; FLASH erase and program are allowed.

fields.name: PRDIV8
fields.text: Divides the FLASH clock by 8 before the divider.

values.text: Divider input is the bus clock.
Divider input is the bus clock divided by 8.

fields.name: DIV
fields.text: FLASH clock divisor: fFCLK = fBus / (DIV + 1) with PRDIV8 = 0, or fBus / (8 x (DIV + 1)) with PRDIV8 = 1. fFCLK must lie between 150 kHz and 200 kHz for FLASH operations; one fFCLK cycle (5 us to 6.7 us) is the program/erase pulse, and erase and program each take a whole number of these pulses.

registers.name: FOPT
registers.title: FLASH Options Register
notes: Reset loads it from NVOPT.
The field table names SEC0 SEC0[1:0].

fields.name: KEYEN
fields.text: Backdoor key mechanism enable. At 0 the backdoor key cannot release security. Only user (secured) firmware can use the key; BDM commands cannot write the key comparison values.

values.text: Security is released until the next MCU reset when user firmware writes 8 bytes matching NVBACKKEY to NVBACKKEY+7, in order.

fields.name: FNORED
fields.text: Vector redirection disable; 1 turns vector redirection off.

fields.name: SEC0
fields.text: Two-bit code for the MCU security state, SEC01:SEC00: 0:0, 0:1 and 1:1 secure; 1:0 unsecured. While secure, no unsecured source, the background debug interface included, can access RAM or FLASH by instructions. SEC01:SEC00 becomes 1:0 after a correct backdoor key entry or a passing FLASH blank check.

fields.name: KEYACC
fields.text: Lets writes go to the backdoor comparison key.

values.text: Writes to 0xFFB0-0xFFB7 start a FLASH program or erase command.
Writes to NVBACKKEY (0xFFB0-0xFFB7) are taken as comparison key writes.

registers.name: FPROT
registers.title: FLASH Protection Register
notes: Reset loads it from NVPROT.

fields.name: FPS
fields.text: With FPDIS = 0, sets the last address of the unprotected FLASH at the top end of FLASH; protected locations cannot be erased or programmed.

fields.name: FPDIS
fields.text: FLASH protection disable.

values.text: The FLASH block set by FPS7:FPS1 is protected from program and erase.

fields.name: FCBEF
fields.text: Launches commands and shows the command buffer is empty for the next command in burst programming. Cleared by writing 1 or when a burst program command moves to the array. Only burst program commands are buffered.

values.text: Command buffer full; no more commands accepted.
Command buffer ready for a new burst program command.

fields.name: FCCF
fields.text: Set by hardware when the command buffer is empty and no command is running; cleared by hardware when a command starts (a 1 written to FCBEF). Writes do nothing.

fields.name: FPVIOL
fields.text: Set by hardware when a command registered by clearing FCBEF tries to erase or program a protected block; that command is ignored. Write 1 to clear.

values.text: Erase or program of a protected location was attempted.

fields.name: FACCERR
fields.text: Set by hardware when the command sequence is broken (the command is ignored), when program or erase is tried before FCDIV is set, or when the MCU enters stop during a command. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FBLANK
fields.text: Set by hardware at the end of a blank check that finds the whole FLASH array erased; cleared when FCBEF is cleared to write a new valid command. Writes do nothing.

values.text: With the blank check done and FCCF = 1: FLASH array not fully erased.
With the blank check done and FCCF = 1: FLASH array fully erased (all 0xFF).

fields.name: FCMD
fields.text: FLASH command code, write only, reads 0. Five codes are accepted in normal user modes: 0x05 blank check, 0x20 byte program, 0x25 burst byte program, 0x40 page erase (512-byte page), 0x41 mass erase (all FLASH). Any other code is illegal and raises an access error. A blank check is not needed after mass erase; it is needed only in the security unlock sequence.

registers.name: NVBACKKEY
notes: Only the register summary gives it.

fields.name: ComparisonKey
fields.text: Eight-byte comparison key at 0xFFB0-0xFFB7, held in FLASH, for the backdoor security release.

registers.name: NVPROT
registers.title: FLASH Protection Register
notes: Reset loads it from NVPROT.
Shares its figure with FPROT.

fields.name: FPS
fields.text: With FPDIS = 0, sets the last address of the unprotected FLASH at the top end of FLASH; protected locations cannot be erased or programmed.

fields.name: FPDIS
fields.text: FLASH protection disable.

values.text: The FLASH block set by FPS7:FPS1 is protected from program and erase.

registers.name: NVOPT
registers.title: FLASH Options Register
notes: Reset loads it from NVOPT.
The field table names SEC0 SEC0[1:0].
Shares its figure with FOPT.

fields.name: KEYEN
fields.text: Backdoor key mechanism enable. At 0 the backdoor key cannot release security. Only user (secured) firmware can use the key; BDM commands cannot write the key comparison values.

values.text: Security is released until the next MCU reset when user firmware writes 8 bytes matching NVBACKKEY to NVBACKKEY+7, in order.

fields.name: FNORED
fields.text: Vector redirection disable; 1 turns vector redirection off.

fields.name: SEC0
fields.text: Two-bit code for the MCU security state, SEC01:SEC00: 0:0, 0:1 and 1:1 secure; 1:0 unsecured. While secure, no unsecured source, the background debug interface included, can access RAM or FLASH by instructions. SEC01:SEC00 becomes 1:0 after a correct backdoor key entry or a passing FLASH blank check.

peripherals.name: SYSTEM
peripherals.title: Resets, Interrupts, and General System Control

registers.name: IRQSC
registers.title: Interrupt Request Status and Control Register

fields.name: IRQPDD
fields.text: Turns off the IRQ pin's internal pullup while the IRQ pin is enabled (IRQPE = 1), so an external pull device can be used.

values.text: IRQ pull device on when IRQPE = 1.
IRQ pull device off when IRQPE = 1.

fields.name: IRQPE
fields.text: Turns on the IRQ pin function so the pin can request interrupts.

fields.name: IRQF
fields.text: Read-only; shows an interrupt request event has happened.

fields.name: IRQACK
fields.text: Write-only; writing 1 clears IRQF, writing 0 does nothing, reads give 0. With edge-and-level detection (IRQMOD = 1), IRQF stays set while the IRQ pin is held at its active level.

fields.name: IRQIE
fields.text: Chooses whether IRQ events request an interrupt.

values.text: No interrupt on IRQF; poll it.

fields.name: IRQMOD
fields.text: Chooses edge-only or edge-and-level detection.

values.text: IRQ event on falling edges only.
IRQ event on a falling edge or while the pin is low.

registers.name: SRS
registers.title: System Reset Status
notes: Any other reset: 0b0xxxx000.
The reset carried is the POR row.

fields.name: POR
fields.text: Reset came from power-on detection. LVD is set too, since the internal supply was still ramping and under the LVR threshold.

fields.name: PIN
fields.text: Reset came from a low level on the external reset pin.

fields.name: COP
fields.text: Reset came from a COP watchdog timeout; COPE = 0 blocks this source.

fields.name: ILOP
fields.text: Reset came from executing an unimplemented or illegal opcode. STOP counts as illegal when STOPE = 0 in SOPT, and BGND when ENBDM = 0 in BDCSC.

fields.name: ILAD
fields.text: Reset came from a data or instruction access to an unimplemented address.

fields.name: LVD
fields.text: Set by an LVD reset (supply below the LVD trip voltage with LVDRE set) and also by POR.

values.text: Not an LVD trip or POR.

registers.name: SBDFR
registers.title: System Background Debug Force Reset Register

fields.name: BDFR
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the MCU; only a debug host can write it, through a background command like WRITE_BYTE, never the user program. PTA4/ACMPO/BKGD/MS high just after the WRITE_BYTE gives user mode; low gives BDM.

fields.name: COPE
fields.text: Write-once; enables the COP watchdog.

values.text: COP watchdog on; a timeout resets the MCU.

fields.name: COPT
fields.text: Write-once; picks the COP timeout, together with COPCLKS in SOPT2.

fields.name: STOPE
fields.text: Write-once; enables stop mode. With stop disabled, a STOP instruction forces an illegal opcode reset.

fields.name: BKGDPE
fields.text: Write-once; gives PTA4/ACMPO/BKGD/MS the BKGD/MS function when set, or one of its output-only functions when clear. Every MCU reset returns the pin to BKGD/MS.

values.text: Pin works as PTA4 or ACMPO.

fields.name: RSTPE
fields.text: Write-once; gives PTA5/IRQ/TCLK/RESET the RESET function when set, with an internal pullup on RESET, or one of its input-only functions when clear. After POR the pin is its input-only port function.

values.text: Pin works as PTA5, IRQ or TCLK.

fields.name: COPCLKS
fields.text: Write-once; picks the COP watchdog clock.

values.text: COP runs from the internal 1 kHz clock.
COP runs from the bus clock.

fields.name: IICPS
fields.text: Picks which pins carry the IIC SDA and SCL.

values.text: SDA on PTA2, SCL on PTA3.
SDA on PTB6, SCL on PTB7.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: Routes the ACMP output to TPM input channel 0.

values.text: ACMP output not routed to TPM channel 0.
ACMP output routed to TPM channel 0.

registers.name: SDIDH
registers.title: System Device Identiﬁcation Register — High
notes: The field table names ID ID[11:8].

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Upper bits of the part identification number, unique to each HCS08 derivative; fixed at 0x009 for the MC9S08QG8.

registers.name: SDIDL
registers.title: System Device Identiﬁcation Register — Low
notes: The field table names ID ID[7:0].

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Lower bits of the part identification number, unique to each HCS08 derivative; fixed at 0x009 for the MC9S08QG8.

registers.name: SRTISC
registers.title: System RTI Status and Control Register

fields.name: RTIF
fields.text: Read-only; shows the periodic wakeup timer has timed out.

values.text: Periodic wakeup timer not timed out.

fields.name: RTIACK
fields.text: Write-only; writing 1 clears RTIF, writing 0 does nothing, reads give 0.

fields.name: RTICLKS
fields.text: Picks the real-time interrupt clock.

fields.name: RTIE
fields.text: Enables real-time interrupts.

fields.name: RTIS
fields.text: Picks the real-time interrupt period, RTIS2:RTIS1:RTIS0. With the internal 1 kHz clock (tRTI = 1 ms): 000 RTI off, 001 8 ms, 010 32 ms, 011 64 ms, 100 128 ms, 101 256 ms, 110 512 ms, 111 1.024 s; the first timeout can be up to one 1 kHz period short. With the external clock, the period is text (the external crystal period) times 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 or 32768 for 001 to 111; 000 turns RTI off.

registers.name: SPMSC1
registers.title: System Power Management Status and Control 1 Register

fields.name: LVDF
fields.text: Read-only; with LVDE = 1, shows a low-voltage detect event.

fields.name: LVDACK
fields.text: Write-only; writing 1 clears LVDF. Reads give 0.

fields.name: LVDIE
fields.text: Enables hardware interrupt requests from LVDF.

fields.name: LVDRE
fields.text: Write-once; with LVDE = 1, lets LVDF events reset the MCU.

values.text: LVDF does not reset the MCU.

fields.name: LVDSE
fields.text: With LVDE = 1, chooses whether low-voltage detect runs in stop mode.

fields.name: LVDE
fields.text: Write-once; turns on the low-voltage detect logic and gates the other bits of this register.

fields.name: BGBE
fields.text: Turns on a buffer for the bandgap reference, used by the ADC on an internal channel or by the ACMP as a reference.

registers.name: SPMSC2
registers.title: System Power Management Status and Control 2 Register

fields.name: PDF
fields.text: Read-only; shows the MCU has come back from stop1.

fields.name: PPDF
fields.text: Read-only; shows the MCU has come back from stop2.

fields.name: PPDACK
fields.text: Writing 1 clears PPDF and PDF.

fields.name: PDC
fields.text: Allows entry to the power-down modes, stop2 and stop1.

fields.name: PPDC
fields.text: Picks which power-down mode is used.

values.text: Stop1 (full power down) when PDC is set.
Stop2 (partial power down) when PDC is set.

registers.name: SPMSC3
registers.title: System Power Management Status and Control 3 Register
notes: LVR: 0b00uu0000.
Any other reset: 0b00uu0000.
The reset carried is the POR row.

fields.name: LVWF
fields.text: Low-voltage warning status.

values.text: Low-voltage warning present now or earlier.

fields.name: LVWACK
fields.text: Writing 1 clears LVWF to 0 when no low-voltage warning is present.

fields.name: LVDV
fields.text: Picks the LVD trip voltage VLVD.

fields.name: LVWV
fields.text: Picks the LVW trip voltage VLVW.

registers.name: PTAD
registers.title: Port A Data Register
notes: The field table names PTAD PTAD[5:0].

fields.name: PTAD
fields.text: Port A data. A read gives the pin level for an input pin and the last value written for an output pin. Writes are latched into every bit and driven onto the pins set as outputs. Reset clears PTAD to 0s, but they are not driven, since reset also makes every port pin a high-impedance input with pullups off.

registers.name: PTADD
registers.title: Port A Data Direction Register
notes: The field table names PTADD PTADD[5:0].

fields.name: PTADD
fields.text: Sets the direction of each port A pin and what a PTAD read returns.

values.text: Input, output driver off; reads give the pin level.
Output driver on for port A bit n; PTAD reads give PTADn.

registers.name: PTBD
registers.title: Port B Data Register
notes: The field table names PTBD PTBD[7:0].

fields.name: PTBD
fields.text: Port B data. A read gives the pin level for an input pin and the last value written for an output pin. Writes are latched into every bit and driven onto the pins set as outputs. Reset clears PTBD to 0s, but they are not driven, since reset also makes every port pin a high-impedance input with pullups off.

registers.name: PTBDD
registers.title: Data Direction for Port B
notes: The field table names PTBDD PTBDD[7:0].

fields.name: PTBDD
fields.text: Sets the direction of each port B pin and what a PTBD read returns.

values.text: Input, output driver off; reads give the pin level.
Output driver on for port B bit n; PTBD reads give PTBDn.

registers.name: PTAPE
registers.title: Internal Pullup Enable for Port A Register
notes: The field table names PTAPE PTAPE[5:0].

fields.name: PTAPE
fields.text: Turns on the internal pullup of each PTA pin. On pins set as outputs these bits do nothing and the pullups are off.

values.text: Pullup off for port A bit n.
Pullup on for port A bit n.

registers.name: PTASE
registers.title: Slew Rate Enable for Port A Register
notes: The field table names PTASE PTASE[5:0].

fields.name: PTASE
fields.text: Turns on output slew rate control for each PTA pin. On pins set as inputs these bits do nothing.

values.text: Slew rate control off for port A bit n.
Slew rate control on for port A bit n.

registers.name: PTADS
registers.title: Drive Strength Selection for Port A Register
notes: The field table names PTADS PTADS[5:0].

fields.name: PTADS
fields.text: Picks low or high output drive for each PTA pin. On pins set as inputs these bits do nothing.

values.text: Low drive for port A bit n.
High drive for port A bit n.

registers.name: PTBPE
registers.title: Internal Pullup Enable for Port B Register
notes: The field table names PTBPE PTBPE[7:0].

fields.name: PTBPE
fields.text: Turns on the internal pullup of each PTB pin. On pins set as outputs these bits do nothing and the pullups are off.

values.text: Pullup off for port B bit n.
Pullup on for port B bit n.

registers.name: PTBSE
registers.title: Slew Rate Enable for Port B Register
notes: The field table names PTBSE PTBSE[7:0].

fields.name: PTBSE
fields.text: Turns on output slew rate control for each PTB pin. On pins set as inputs these bits do nothing.

values.text: Slew rate control off for port B bit n.
Slew rate control on for port B bit n.

registers.name: PTBDS
registers.title: Drive Strength Selection for Port B Register
notes: The field table names PTBDS PTBDS[7:0].

fields.name: PTBDS
fields.text: Picks low or high output drive for each PTB pin. On pins set as inputs these bits do nothing.

values.text: Low drive for port B bit n.
High drive for port B bit n.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Turns on the ACMP module.

fields.name: ACBGS
fields.text: Picks the bandgap reference or the ACMP+ pin for the comparator's non-inverting input.

values.text: ACMP+ pin on the non-inverting input.
Internal reference on the non-inverting input.

fields.name: ACF
fields.text: Set on a compare event, as chosen by ACMOD; write 1 to clear.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: Enables the ACMP interrupt, asserted when ACF is set.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Reads the present comparator output; reset to 0 and reads 0 while ACME = 0.

fields.name: ACOPE
fields.text: Puts the comparator output on the ACMPO pin.

fields.name: ACMOD
fields.text: Picks which comparator output change sets ACF.

fields.name: COCO
fields.text: Read-only. With the compare function off (ACFE = 0) it sets at the end of every conversion; with it on (ACFE = 1) only when the compare result is true. Cleared by a write to ADCSC1 or a read of ADCRL.

fields.name: AIEN
fields.text: Enables the conversion complete interrupt, asserted when COCO sets with AIEN high.

fields.name: ADCO
fields.text: Enables continuous conversions.

values.text: One conversion per ADCSC1 write (software trigger) or per ADHWT assertion (hardware trigger).
Conversions repeat, starting from an ADCSC1 write (software trigger) or an ADHWT event (hardware trigger).

fields.name: ADCH
fields.text: Five-bit input channel select. All 1s turns off the converter and isolates the input from every source, and ends continuous conversion without one more conversion. All 1s is not needed for low power outside continuous mode: the module enters a low-power state by itself when a conversion ends.

fields.name: ADACT
fields.text: Shows a conversion is running: set when one starts, cleared when it finishes or is aborted.

fields.name: ADTRG
fields.text: Picks the conversion trigger: software, where a write to ADCSC1 starts a conversion, or hardware, where ADHWT assertion starts it.

fields.name: ACFE
fields.text: Turns on the compare function.

fields.name: ACFGT
fields.text: Makes the compare trigger when the result is at or above the compare value; otherwise it triggers when the result is below it.

values.text: Triggers when the input is below the compare level.
Triggers when the input is at or above the compare level.

fields.name: ADR9
fields.text: Bit 9 of a 10-bit conversion result; reads 0 in 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR8
fields.text: Bit 8 of a 10-bit conversion result; reads 0 in 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR7
fields.text: Bit 7 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR6
fields.text: Bit 6 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR5
fields.text: Bit 5 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR4
fields.text: Bit 4 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR3
fields.text: Bit 3 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR2
fields.text: Bit 2 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR1
fields.text: Bit 1 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADR0
fields.text: Bit 0 of the conversion result, in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV9
fields.text: Bit 9 of the 10-bit compare value, matched against the result's upper bits in 10-bit mode with compare on; unused in 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV8
fields.text: Bit 8 of the 10-bit compare value, matched against the result's upper bits in 10-bit mode with compare on; unused in 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV7
fields.text: Bit 7 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV6
fields.text: Bit 6 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV5
fields.text: Bit 5 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV4
fields.text: Bit 4 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV3
fields.text: Bit 3 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV2
fields.text: Bit 2 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV1
fields.text: Bit 1 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADCV0
fields.text: Bit 0 of the compare value, matched against the result's lower 8 bits in 10-bit or 8-bit mode.

fields.name: ADLPC
fields.text: Trades converter speed against power, to save power when high sample rates are not needed.

values.text: Low power; lower maximum clock speed.

fields.name: ADIV
fields.text: Divide ratio from the input clock to the internal ADC clock ADCK: 00 divide by 1, 01 by 2, 10 by 4, 11 by 8.

fields.name: ADLSMP
fields.text: Picks a long or short sample time: longer for higher-impedance inputs or lower power in continuous conversion, shorter for faster conversion of low-impedance inputs.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Picks the conversion resolution: 00 8-bit (N = 8), 10 10-bit (N = 10); 01 and 11 reserved.

fields.name: ADICLK
fields.text: Picks the input clock from which ADCK is made: 00 the bus clock, 01 half the bus clock, 10 ALTCLK, the alternate clock, 11 ADACK, the asynchronous clock.

fields.name: ADPC7
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD7.

fields.name: ADPC6
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD6.

fields.name: ADPC5
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD5.

fields.name: ADPC4
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD4.

fields.name: ADPC3
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD3.

fields.name: ADPC2
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD2.

fields.name: ADPC1
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD1.

fields.name: ADPC0
fields.text: Controls the pin of ADC channel AD0.

fields.name: CLKS
fields.text: Picks the clock that sets the bus frequency, which is then divided by BDIV.

fields.name: RDIV
fields.text: Divides the FLL reference clock picked by IREFS; the result must be 31.25 kHz to 39.0625 kHz.

fields.name: IREFS
fields.text: Picks the FLL reference clock.

fields.name: IRCLKEN
fields.text: Turns on the internal reference clock as ICSIRCLK.

fields.name: IREFSTEN
fields.text: Chooses whether the internal reference clock keeps running when the ICS enters stop.

values.text: Internal reference keeps running in stop if IRCLKEN is set or the ICS was in FEI, FBI or FBILP before stop.

fields.name: BDIV
fields.text: Divides the clock picked by CLKS to set the bus frequency.

fields.name: RANGE
fields.text: Picks the external oscillator frequency range.

fields.name: HGO
fields.text: Sets the external oscillator's operating mode.

fields.name: LP
fields.text: Chooses whether the FLL is turned off in the FLL bypassed modes.

values.text: FLL off in bypass modes unless BDM is active.
FLL stays on in bypass modes.

fields.name: EREFS
fields.text: Picks the source of the external reference clock.

fields.name: ERCLKEN
fields.text: Turns on the external reference clock as ICSERCLK.

fields.name: EREFSTEN
fields.text: Chooses whether the external reference clock keeps running when the ICS enters stop.

values.text: External reference keeps running in stop if ERCLKEN is set or the ICS was in FEE, FBE or FBELP before stop.

registers.name: ICSTRM
registers.title: ICS Trim Register
notes: Reset: 0buuuuuuuu.
The reset carried is the POR row.

fields.name: TRIM
fields.text: Trims the internal reference clock period, bits binary weighted: a larger value gives a longer period, a smaller one a shorter period. FTRIM in ICSSC adds one finer step.

registers.name: ICSSC
registers.title: ICS Status and Control Register
notes: Reset: 0b0000000u.
The reset carried is the POR row.

fields.name: CLKST
fields.text: Present clock mode. It lags a write to CLKS because of synchronisation between clock domains.

fields.name: OSCINIT
fields.text: Set when the external oscillator finishes its start-up cycles, provided EREFS is set and the external reference is in use through ERCLKEN or FEE, FBE or FBELP mode. Cleared only when ERCLKEN or EREFS is cleared.

fields.name: FTRIM
fields.text: Smallest trim step of the internal reference clock: 1 lengthens the period, 0 shortens it.

registers.name: IICA
registers.title: IIC Address Register
notes: The field table names ADDR ADDR[7:1].

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Slave address the IIC module answers to when addressed as a slave.

fields.name: MULT
fields.text: Sets the multiplier mul, used with the SCL divider to make the IIC baud rate.

fields.name: ICR
fields.text: Prescales the bus clock for the bit rate; it fixes the SCL divider and also the SDA hold value. Baud rate = bus frequency (Hz) / (mul x SCL divider). SDA hold time, from SCL falling to SDA changing, = bus period (s) x SDA hold value.

fields.name: IICEN
fields.text: Turns on the IIC module.

fields.name: IICIE
fields.text: Enables the IIC interrupt request.

fields.name: MST
fields.text: Going from 0 to 1 generates a START on the bus and selects master mode; going from 1 to 0 generates a STOP and returns to slave mode.

fields.name: TX
fields.text: Transfer direction, for master and slave. As master it is set for the transfer wanted and is high for address cycles; as an addressed slave, software sets it from SRW.

fields.name: TXAK
fields.text: Level driven on SDA in data acknowledge cycles, for master and slave receivers.

values.text: Acknowledge sent after each received byte.

fields.name: RSTA
fields.text: Writing 1 generates a repeated START when the module is the current master. Always reads 0. A repeat at the wrong time loses arbitration.

fields.name: TCF
fields.text: Set when a byte transfer finishes; valid only during or just after a transfer to or from the IIC module. Cleared by reading IICD in receive mode or writing IICD in transmit mode.

fields.name: IAAS
fields.text: Set when the calling address matches the module's own address; cleared by a write to IICC.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Bus state in either mode: set on a detected START, cleared on a detected STOP.

fields.name: ARBL
fields.text: Set by hardware when arbitration is lost; software clears it by writing 1.

fields.name: SRW
fields.text: As an addressed slave, the R/W bit of the calling address.

values.text: Slave receive; master writes to the slave.
Slave transmit; master reads from the slave.

fields.name: IICIF
fields.text: Set when an interrupt is pending: a byte transfer finishes, the slave address matches the calling address, or arbitration is lost. Software clears it by writing 1, in the interrupt routine.

fields.name: RXAK
fields.text: Low when an acknowledge was received after a byte was sent on the bus; high when none was detected.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: IIC data. In master transmit, a write starts a transfer, MSB first; in master receive, a read starts reception of the next byte. Leave master receive before reading IICD so as not to start an unwanted receive. As a slave the same functions apply after an address match. TX in IICC must match the transfer direction for a transfer to start. A read gives the last byte received in master or slave receive; IICD does not show every byte on the bus and cannot be read back to check a write. In master transmit, the first byte written after MST is asserted carries the calling address in bits 7-1 and the R/W bit in bit 0.

fields.name: KBF
fields.text: Shows a keyboard interrupt was detected; writes do not change it.

fields.name: KBACK
fields.text: Writing 1 is part of clearing KBF. Reads give 0.

fields.name: KBIE
fields.text: Enables the keyboard interrupt request.

fields.name: KBMOD
fields.text: With the KBEDG bits, sets how the keyboard interrupt pins are detected.

fields.name: KBIPEn
fields.text: Each bit enables its keyboard interrupt pin.

fields.name: KBEDGn
fields.text: Each bit picks, for its pin, detection on falling edges and low levels or on rising edges and high levels.

fields.name: TOF
fields.text: Read-only flag that goes to 1 when the MTIM counter wraps to 0x00 after reaching the MTIMMOD value. Cleared by reading MTIMSC with TOF at 1 and then writing 0 to TOF, by writing 1 to TRST, or by any write to MTIMMOD.

values.text: Counter has not reached the MTIMMOD overflow value.
Counter has reached the MTIMMOD overflow value.

fields.name: TOIE
fields.text: Read/write enable for the MTIM overflow interrupt: when 1, TOF = 1 raises an interrupt. Cleared by reset. Clear TOF before setting TOIE; do not set it while TOF = 1.

values.text: TOF interrupt off; TOF is polled in software.

fields.name: TRST
fields.text: Write-only: writing 1 sets the MTIM counter to 0x00 and clears TOF. Always reads 0.

values.text: No effect; the counter keeps its value.

fields.name: TSTP
fields.text: Read/write: 1 holds the MTIM counter at its present value; clearing it lets counting carry on from that value. Reset sets TSTP, so the MTIM does not count after reset.

fields.name: CLKS
fields.text: Read/write pair choosing which of four clocks feeds the MTIM prescaler. A change while counting leaves the count as it is and counting goes on from the new clock. Reset sets 00.

fields.name: PS
fields.text: Read/write, picks one of nine taps of the 8-bit prescaler. A change while counting leaves the count as it is and counting goes on at the new rate. Reset sets 0000. Codes not listed give the clock source divided by 256.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Read-only present value of the 8-bit MTIM counter; writes do nothing. Reset sets 0x00.

fields.name: MOD
fields.text: Read/write value at which the count resets and TOF is set; 0x00 makes the MTIM free-running. A write to MTIMMOD sets COUNT to 0x00 and clears TOF. Reset sets 0x00.

registers.name: SCIBDH
registers.title: SCI Baud Rate Register
notes: The field table names SBR SBR[12:8].

fields.name: SBR
fields.text: Upper five bits of the 13-bit baud divisor BR (SBR[12:0] across SCIBDH and SCIBDL). BR = 0 turns the SCI baud generator off to save supply current; BR = 1 to 8191 gives a baud rate of BUSCLK/(16 x BR).

registers.name: SCIBDL
registers.title: SCI Baud Rate Register
notes: The field table names SBR SBR[7:0].

fields.name: SBR
fields.text: Lower eight bits of the 13-bit baud divisor BR (SBR[12:0] across SCIBDH and SCIBDL). BR = 0 turns the SCI baud generator off to save supply current; BR = 1 to 8191 gives a baud rate of BUSCLK/(16 x BR).

fields.name: LOOPS
fields.text: Chooses loop-back operation or normal full-duplex operation on two pins. With LOOPS = 1 the transmitter output feeds the receiver input inside the SCI.

values.text: Normal: RxD and TxD are separate pins.
Loop or single-wire mode, set by RSRC: transmitter output tied to receiver input inside the SCI; the SCI does not use the RxD pin.

fields.name: SCISWAI
fields.text: SCI stops in wait mode.

values.text: SCI clocks keep running in wait mode, so an SCI interrupt can wake the CPU.
SCI clocks halt while the CPU is in wait mode.

fields.name: RSRC
fields.text: Only acts when LOOPS = 1. Then the receiver input is tied internally to the TxD pin, and RSRC chooses whether that node is also tied to the transmitter output.

values.text: With LOOPS = 1: internal loop-back; the SCI does not use RxD.
Single-wire mode: the TxD pin carries both transmitter output and receiver input.

fields.name: M
fields.text: 9-bit or 8-bit character select.

values.text: Start bit, 8 data bits LSB first, stop bit.
Start bit, 8 data bits LSB first, a ninth data bit, stop bit, for both receiver and transmitter.

fields.name: WAKE
fields.text: Chooses how the receiver wakes from standby.

fields.name: ILT
fields.text: When 1, the stop bit and trailing 1 bits of a character are not counted toward the 10 or 11 high bit times the idle-line detector looks for.

values.text: Idle bit count begins after the start bit.
Idle bit count begins after the stop bit.

fields.name: PE
fields.text: Turns on hardware parity generation and checking. The top bit of the character (the eighth or ninth data bit) then serves as the parity bit.

fields.name: PT
fields.text: With PE = 1, chooses even or odd parity: the count of 1s in the character, parity bit included, is even or odd to match.

fields.name: TIE
fields.text: Transmit interrupt enable, for TDRE.

values.text: TDRE interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: TCIE
fields.text: Transmission-complete interrupt enable, for TC.

values.text: TC interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: RIE
fields.text: Receiver interrupt enable, for RDRF.

values.text: RDRF interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: ILIE
fields.text: Idle-line interrupt enable, for IDLE.

values.text: IDLE interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: TE
fields.text: Transmitter enable; must be 1 to use the SCI transmitter. With TE = 1 the SCI normally drives TxD as an output, but with LOOPS = 1 and RSRC = 0 TxD goes back to port B general-purpose I/O even with TE = 1. In single-wire mode (LOOPS = RSRC = 1) TXDIR sets the direction on TxD. Writing TE = 0 then TE = 1 during a transmission queues an idle character. After TE is written 0, the transmitter holds TxD until queued data, idle or break finishes sending, then the pin returns to general-purpose I/O.

fields.name: RE
fields.text: Turns the SCI receiver on or off. With the receiver off, RxD returns to general-purpose port I/O.

fields.name: RWU
fields.text: Writing 1 puts the receiver in standby until hardware sees the wakeup condition chosen by WAKE: an idle line between messages (WAKE = 0) or a 1 in the top data bit of a character (WAKE = 1). Software sets RWU; the chosen hardware condition normally clears it.

values.text: Receiver in standby until the wakeup condition.

fields.name: SBK
fields.text: Writing 1 then 0 queues one break character for transmission. While SBK stays 1, more breaks of 10 or 11 bit times of 0 are queued; depending on when SBK is set and cleared against the data being sent, a second break may be queued before software clears it.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Set at reset and whenever a value moves from the transmit buffer to the transmit shifter, freeing the buffer for a new character. Cleared by reading SCIS1 with TDRE = 1 and then writing SCID.

fields.name: TC
fields.text: Set at reset and when TDRE = 1 with no data, preamble or break being sent. Cleared by reading SCIS1 with TC = 1 and then either writing SCID with new data, queuing a preamble by taking TE from 0 to 1, or queuing a break by writing 1 to SBK in SCIC2.

values.text: Transmitter busy sending data, a preamble or a break.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Set when a character moves from the receive shifter into SCID. Cleared by reading SCIS1 with RDRF = 1 and then reading SCID.

fields.name: IDLE
fields.text: Set when the receive line has been idle for one full character time after activity. With ILT = 0 idle bit times are counted from the start bit, so the 1 bits and stop bit of an all-ones character count toward the 10 or 11 high bit times (set by M) needed; with ILT = 1 counting begins after the stop bit, so trailing high bits and the stop bit of the last character do not count. Cleared by reading SCIS1 with IDLE = 1 and then reading SCID. Once cleared, IDLE cannot set again until a new character has arrived and set RDRF; it sets only once however long the line stays idle.

fields.name: OR
fields.text: Set when a fresh character is waiting to enter SCID but the last one has not been read yet; the fresh character and its error information are lost. Cleared by reading SCIS1 with OR = 1 and then reading SCID.

fields.name: NF
fields.text: The receiver samples the start bit seven times and each data bit and the stop bit three times; if any sample in a bit time disagrees with the others, NF is set together with RDRF for that character. Cleared by reading SCIS1 and then reading SCID.

values.text: Noise seen in the character in SCID.

fields.name: FE
fields.text: Set together with RDRF when the receiver finds a 0 where the stop bit should be, a sign that it was out of step with the character frame. Cleared by reading SCIS1 with FE = 1 and then reading SCID.

values.text: No framing error seen; framing is not thereby confirmed correct.

fields.name: PF
fields.text: Set together with RDRF when PE = 1 and the received parity bit does not match the expected parity. Cleared by reading SCIS1 and then reading SCID.

fields.name: BRK13
fields.text: Selects a longer break character. Framing error detection is the same either way.

values.text: Break is 10 bit times, 11 with M = 1.
Break is 13 bit times, 14 with M = 1.

fields.name: RAF
fields.text: Set when the receiver sees the start of a valid start bit; cleared by hardware when it sees an idle line. Can be checked to see whether a character is arriving before the MCU is put in stop mode.

values.text: Receiver idle, waiting for a start bit.

fields.name: R8
fields.text: In 9-bit mode (M = 1), the ninth received data bit, sitting above the MSB of SCID. Read R8 before SCID: reading SCID finishes the flag-clearing sequences, after which new data can overwrite R8 and SCID.

fields.name: T8
fields.text: In 9-bit mode (M = 1), the ninth transmit data bit, sitting above the MSB of SCID. All nine bits go to the shifter once SCID is written, so write T8 first when it must change; if it stays the same (for example when used for mark or space parity), there is no need to rewrite it on each SCID write.

fields.name: TXDIR
fields.text: Sets the direction of data on TxD in single-wire half-duplex mode (LOOPS = RSRC = 1).

fields.name: TXINV
fields.text: 1 inverts the polarity of the transmitted data.

fields.name: ORIE
fields.text: Lets the overrun flag OR request a hardware interrupt.

values.text: OR interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: NEIE
fields.text: Lets the noise flag NF request a hardware interrupt.

values.text: NF interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: FEIE
fields.text: Lets the framing error flag FE request a hardware interrupt.

values.text: FE interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: PEIE
fields.text: Lets the parity error flag PF request a hardware interrupt.

values.text: PF interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: R7
fields.text: Bit 7 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T7
fields.text: Bit 7 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R6
fields.text: Bit 6 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T6
fields.text: Bit 6 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R5
fields.text: Bit 5 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T5
fields.text: Bit 5 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R4
fields.text: Bit 4 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T4
fields.text: Bit 4 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R3
fields.text: Bit 3 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T3
fields.text: Bit 3 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R2
fields.text: Bit 2 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T2
fields.text: Bit 2 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R1
fields.text: Bit 1 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T1
fields.text: Bit 1 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: R0
fields.text: Bit 0 of the read-only receive data buffer; a read of SCID returns it. SCID reads also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: T0
fields.text: Bit 0 of the write-only transmit data buffer; a write to SCID goes to it. SCID writes also take part in clearing the SCI status flags.

fields.name: SPIE
fields.text: Interrupt enable for the receive-buffer-full flag SPRF and the mode-fault flag MODF.

values.text: SPRF and MODF interrupts off; poll the flags.
SPRF or MODF at 1 requests an interrupt.

fields.name: SPE
fields.text: Turns the SPI on. Turning it off stops any transfer under way, empties the data buffers and resets the internal state machines; SPRF clears and SPTEF sets to show an empty transmit buffer.

fields.name: SPTIE
fields.text: Interrupt enable for the transmit-buffer-empty flag SPTEF.

values.text: SPTEF interrupt off; poll the flag.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: Master or slave mode select.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Inverts the SPI clock, whether sent by a master or received by a slave.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Chooses between two SPI clock formats, to suit different synchronous serial devices.

values.text: First SPSCK edge in the middle of the first of the 8 transfer cycles.
First SPSCK edge at the start of the first of the 8 transfer cycles.

fields.name: SSOE
fields.text: Together with MODFEN in SPIC2 and MSTR, decides what the SS pin does. In master mode: MODFEN = 0 makes SS general-purpose I/O outside the SPI whatever SSOE is; MODFEN = 1 with SSOE = 0 makes SS the mode-fault input, with SSOE = 1 an automatic slave-select output. In slave mode SS is always the slave select input.

fields.name: LSBFE
fields.text: LSB first; sets the shifter direction.

fields.name: MODFEN
fields.text: In slave mode it does nothing, SS being the slave select input. In master mode it decides how the SS pin is used.

values.text: Mode fault off; in master mode SS is general-purpose I/O outside SPI control.
Mode fault on; in master mode SS serves as mode-fault input or as slave-select output.

fields.name: BIDIROE
fields.text: With single-wire bidirectional mode on (SPC0 = 1), turns the SPI data output driver on the one data pin on or off: MOSI (MOMI) for a master, MISO (SISO) for a slave. Does nothing when SPC0 = 0.

values.text: Driver off; the data pin is an input.

fields.name: SPISWAI
fields.text: SPI stops in wait mode.

values.text: SPI clocks keep running in wait mode.
SPI clocks halt when the MCU enters wait mode.

fields.name: SPC0
fields.text: Selects single-wire bidirectional mode. A slave (MSTR = 0) then moves data on MISO (SISO), a master (MSTR = 1) on MOSI (MOMI). With SPC0 = 1, BIDIROE turns the output driver on that pin on or off.

values.text: Separate data input and output pins.

registers.name: SPIBR
registers.title: SPI Baud Rate Register
notes: The field table names SPPR SPPR[2:0].
The field table names SPR SPR[2:0].

fields.name: SPPR
fields.text: 3-bit field selecting the SPI baud prescaler divisor: code 000 to 111 divides by 1 to 8 (code plus one). Its input is BUSCLK and its output feeds the SPI baud rate divider.

fields.name: SPR
fields.text: 3-bit field selecting the SPI baud rate divider's divisor: 000 /2, 001 /4, 010 /8, 011 /16, 100 /32, 101 /64, 110 /128, 111 /256. Its input comes from the prescaler; its output is the master-mode bit rate clock.

fields.name: SPRF
fields.text: Set when an SPI transfer completes, meaning received data can be read from SPID. Cleared by reading SPRF while it is 1 and then reading SPID.

fields.name: SPTEF
fields.text: Set when the transmit buffer has room. Cleared by reading SPIS with SPTEF = 1 and then writing a value to SPID; a write to SPID without that read of SPIS is ignored. With SPTIE in SPIC1 set, SPTEF requests an interrupt. It sets again whenever a byte moves from the buffer to the shift register. On an idle SPI, a byte written to SPID moves to the shifter at once and SPTEF sets within two bus cycles, so a second byte can be queued; when the shifter finishes, the queued byte moves in and SPTEF sets again. With nothing queued, SPTEF stays set and nothing moves.

fields.name: MODF
fields.text: Set when the SPI is a master and its slave select input goes low, meaning another device is also acting as master. SS is a mode-fault input only with MSTR = 1, MODFEN = 1 and SSOE = 0; otherwise MODF never sets. Cleared by reading MODF while it is 1 and then writing SPIC1.

registers.name: TPMSC
registers.title: Timer Status and Control Register
notes: The field table names CLKS CLKS[B:A].
The field table names PS PS[2:0].

fields.name: TOF
fields.text: Set when the TPM counter goes to 0x0000 after reaching the modulo value; in CPWM mode, set when the counter, having reached the modulo value, steps to the next lower count. Cleared by reading TPMSC with TOF set and then writing 0 to TOF; if another overflow comes before that sequence is done, the sequence restarts and TOF stays set. Cleared by reset; writing 1 does nothing.

values.text: Counter has not reached the modulo value or overflowed.

fields.name: TOIE
fields.text: Read/write enable for the TPM overflow interrupt: when 1, TOF = 1 raises an interrupt. Cleared by reset.

values.text: TOF interrupt off; poll in software.

fields.name: CPWMS
fields.text: Read/write selection of center-aligned PWM. Reset clears it, so the TPM counts up, serving edge-aligned PWM, output compare and input capture; when set, the counter counts up and down for CPWM.

values.text: Each channel works in the mode its own MSnB:MSnA bits choose: edge-aligned PWM, output compare or input capture.

fields.name: CLKS
fields.text: 2-bit field that turns the TPM off or picks one of three clocks feeding the counter's prescaler: 00 no clock (TPM off), 01 BUSCLK, 10 XCLK, 11 external TPMCLK, at most a quarter of the bus frequency. XCLK and the external clock are synchronized to the bus clock on chip. With the external clock shared with channel n, that channel's ELSnB:ELSnA is set to 0:0 so the pin has one function.

fields.name: PS
fields.text: 3-bit field selecting the TPM clock input divisor: 000 /1, 001 /2, 010 /4, 011 /8, 100 /16, 101 /32, 110 /64, 111 /128. The prescaler comes after clock selection and synchronization, so it divides whichever clock is chosen.

registers.name: TPMCnSC
registers.title: Timer Channel n Status and Control Register
notes: The field table names ELSn ELSn[B:A].

fields.name: CHnF
fields.text: In input capture, set when an active edge arrives on the channel pin; in output compare or edge-aligned PWM, set when the TPM counter equals the channel value registers. In center-aligned PWM it sets on every match, at both edges of the active duty period, so it is little used there. With CHnIE = 1 it requests an interrupt. Cleared by reading TPMCnSC with CHnF set and then writing 0 to CHnF; another request before that sequence is done restarts it and CHnF stays set, so no request is lost. Cleared by reset; writing 1 does nothing.

values.text: No input capture or output compare event on the channel.
Input capture or output compare event on the channel.

fields.name: CHnIE
fields.text: Read/write enable for the channel's interrupt. Cleared by reset.

values.text: Channel interrupt off; poll in software.

fields.name: MSnB
fields.text: With CPWMS = 0, MSnB = 1 puts the channel in edge-aligned PWM mode.

fields.name: MSnA
fields.text: With CPWMS = 0 and MSnB = 0, MSnA picks input capture or output compare for the channel.

fields.name: ELSn
fields.text: Depending on the channel mode set by CPWMS:MSnB:MSnA, picks the input edge that triggers a capture, the level driven on an output compare match, or the PWM output polarity. ELSnB:ELSnA = 0:0 leaves the pin as general-purpose I/O with no channel function, as used to pause an input capture channel, to free the pin for a channel used as a software timer, or for channel 0 when TPMCH0 is the external clock input.

fields.name: ARM

fields.name: TAG

fields.name: BRKEN

fields.name: RWA

fields.name: RWAEN

fields.name: RWB

fields.name: RWBEN

fields.name: TRGSEL

fields.name: BEGIN

fields.name: TRG2

fields.name: TRG1

fields.name: TRG0

fields.name: ARMF
